name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+16 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent
Stutzman's large fundraising and outside-support edge over Thompson
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 5%
No public polling to challenge the fundamentals-based picture
model.rationale: The R+16 district lean, Stutzman's incumbency and roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing Democrats near 5% all point the same direction, with no polling or ratings suggesting an upset. The forecast stays at a Safe R margin near -16.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Thompson within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Stutzman, would warrant moving this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northeast Indiana's third district is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+16, and incumbent Marlin Stutzman is running for re-election after easily securing his party's nomination. Democrat Kelly Thompson faces steep structural odds in a district that has consistently favored Republicans in recent cycles.

Stutzman holds a clear financial edge, raising roughly $840,000 to Thompson's $136,000, and benefits from modest outside support while facing none in opposition. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 5% chance. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all align on a comfortable Republican win, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
